text:
Marta Álvarez: Quick share — ran a multi-region perf sweep for llm-13b-ql4 (int4) across us-east / us-west / eu-west. Goal: understand p50/p95 delta and how edge routing is adding tail. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/bench/175234 :eyes:
perf-bot: automated run summary attached (run id br-03-10-09). Baseline traffic pattern = 1rps per path, synthetic token length=256, concurrency=32.
perf-bot: ```
Region   GPU   p50(ms)  p95(ms)  GPU%  notes
us-east  H100   78       220      72   direct origin
us-west  H100  130       420      65   edge-pop -> origin crossover adds ~80-120ms
eu-west  A100  110       300      68   steady but higher variance
us-east  L4     95       270      55   cheaper, more variance on p95
```
Kewei Chen: Nice. Two quick things: 1) Did you try flash_attn / fused KV on H100? That drops p50 by ~10-15ms in our microbenchmarks. 2) Batching distribution matters — continuous batching helped reduce GPU% but increased p95 for bursty paths.
Marta Álvarez: I ran with runtime kernels=auto. Didn't force flash_attn. Batching target=64 with max-latency-slo=200ms for the run.
Eli Park: On routing: are requests served from edge POP in the same region or proxied to us-east origin? If proxied, that explains the ~80-120ms penalty for us-west. Also check TLS handshake reuse at the edge.
Anna S.: Confirming — our current CloudFront config points to us-east origin for model-hosting. Edge cache not caching dynamic generative responses so most requests cross-region.
Kewei Chen: Suggestion: two parallel experiments: (A) enable flash_attn + kernel=fused_kv on H100, (B) enable geo-origin routing so eu-west & us-west hit local origin (dedicated pool) — measure p95 delta.
Marta Álvarez: Agreed. I kicked off both experiments. Quick notes/metrics from the first 60min canary:
perf-bot: canary br-03-10-09-canaryA results: H100 + flash_attn -> p50 66ms, p95 190ms (us-east). Cross-region us-west still p50 112ms p95 260ms when origin local.
Kewei Chen: Good sign that kernel change helps origin latency. The remaining us-west tail suggests network + edge TLS + headroom on GPU queues.
Anna S.: For capacity sizing, if we want p95 <= 250ms in us-west at 95th percentile of load, we should increase concurrency pool from 32->48 on the us-west H100 cluster and add 2 more instances behind the LB. That reduces queueing and amortizes TLS.
Eli Park: Also try keepalive pools between edge and origin, and TLS session reuse — that reduced ~30-40ms in previous tests.
Marta Álvarez: Action items: 1) Kewei to push kernel flag change to runtime config (canary on H100, tag v0.48-ker1). 2) Anna to prototype geo-origin routing rule for us-west/eu-west and create infra PR for +2 instances in us-west. 3) Eli to validate TLS keepalive between edge and origin. I'll re-run full sweep after changes and post new dashboard.
Kewei Chen: I'll open the runtime PR and include microbench numbers (flash_attn vs default).
Anna S.: I'll draft infra PR with expected cost delta and capacity plan.
Marta Álvarez: One more datapoint — L4 looks attractive cost-wise but more jitter on p95; we should keep L4 as fallback for non-latency-critical workloads.
Eli Park: Agreed. For customer-facing low-latency SLAs, prefer H100 w/ geo routing + kernel optimizations. L4 for batch/async.
Marta Álvarez: Thanks all — I'll follow up with a 24h canary and then a 3-day smoke to validate p95 stability. Posting results here once done :chart_with_upwards_trend:
